subject: Request: Bridge endorsement to cover SOC 2 Type II post-report period
messages:
From: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@lyricatx.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: compliance@lyricatx.com
Date: 2026-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request for post-report bridge endorsement to cover SOC 2 gap

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the conversation yesterday. As part of Lyrica Therapeutics' procurement checklist, our security team needs a short bridge/endorsement that covers the period after your SOC 2 Type II report end date (2025-12-31) up to our anticipated contract start (2026-06-30).

Specifically, can Redwood provide either:
- a bridge letter confirming there were no material control changes since 2025-12-31 and that controls remain in scope, or
- an interim affirmation of continuity that we can present to our InfoSec team while you finalize the next attestation?

Also curious whether you can include confirmation around: KMS usage for customer data encryption, log retention windows, and whether any control exceptions exist since the report end date.

We have an internal procurement deadline of 2026-05-10 for evidence to advance to SOW signature. Is a short-form bridge doable by then? If you can share a draft, that would speed review.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Hargreaves
Head of Vendor Risk, Lyrica Therapeutics
compliance@lyricatx.com

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Date: 2026-05-01T10:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request for post-report bridge endorsement to cover SOC 2 gap

Hi Tom — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. We can definitely provide a short bridge endorsement. A few clarifying points so we deliver what your InfoSec needs:

1) Desired scope: do you need an assertion of "no material control changes" or a statement confirming controls in scope remained in place? We can do either; the wording differs slightly.
2) KMS confirmation: we can confirm Redwood uses CMEK/KMS for customer keys where enabled and can describe default server-side encryption behavior. If you need HSM attestation language, we should know the exact phrasing required.
3) Evidence: would a one-page bridge letter + an appendix with a KMS key lifecycle summary and log retention table be sufficient?

We’ll loop legal for sign-off on wording and produce a draft by end-of-day 2026-05-04 to meet your 2026-05-10 deadline. Laura — can you take point on the bridge wording? Karthik, please prepare the KMS/log retention appendix.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra

Hi Rishi/Laura,

Thanks — quick clarification from our side: the procurement team prefers (1) a bridge letter that states there have been no material changes to controls affecting the Trust Services Criteria since 2025-12-31, and (2) a short appendix confirming key management and log retention windows (we only need high-level language). We do not require HSM key ceremony details, but confirmation of whether CMEK is available and typical rotation/retention cadence is helpful.

If you can get a draft completed by 2026-05-04 we're happy to review and provide a redline prior to procurement deadline on 2026-05-10.

Appreciate it,
Tom (on behalf of Compliance)

Date: 2026-05-05T16:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request for post-report bridge endorsement to cover SOC 2 gap

Tom — attaching a draft bridge endorsement and a short appendix addressing KMS and log retention. Key points called out in the draft:
- Redwood's last SOC 2 Type II period ended 2025-12-31.
- No material control changes affecting the scope of the report were made between 2026-01-01 and 2026-05-05.
- Redwood supports customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) for Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted customers have server-side encryption with AWS-managed keys unless CMEK is purchased/configured.
- Log retention: security logs retained for 13 months by default; access logs retained for 12 months.

Please find attachments:
- Lyrica_Bridge_Letter_Draft.pdf (bridge endorsement draft)
- Redwood_SOC2_T2_Summary.xlsx (appendix: KMS + log retention table)

Laura — legal approved the template language with one minor edit (typical non-reliance clause). I've embedded that edit in the draft. If you can confirm acceptance, we can sign/execute via DocuSign and I’ll route to Tom for Lyrica procurement.

Next steps:
1) Tom — review and confirm if the language meets procurement needs or if you have edits; we can accommodate small redlines.
2) If accepted, I’ll start a DocuSign flow and aim to have the signed copy to you by 2026-05-07.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
